title: BDF11 10-round AES-128 Automated single-byte fault recovery

target.description: Full AES-128, single unknown-byte fault at X7[0], before final three rounds. Source demonstrates with finalMC included but explicitly says replayable for standard omitted-finalMC.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.plaintext_model: Source-defined plaintext/ciphertext observations under the same key.

fault_model.timing: Before SB of round8 in one-based indexing, state X7 in zero-based source.
fault_model.value_control: Unknown byte difference, not chosen value.
fault_model.sample_pairing: One correct/faulty ciphertext pair for the same plaintext and key.

time.note: Table2 uses encryption units; Section5.3 solver complexity24 is a component operation estimate, and a couple-of-seconds software example is not a new universal runtime.

data.note: One useful fault with correct counterpart; total physical attempts not priced.

preprocessing.note: No numerical amount is reported for this resource.

success.description: The source reports an implemented fault attack and the expected2^16 tested candidates, but no number of attack trials, population success fraction or probability of unique correct-key recovery. The counts2^16/2^24 describe intermediate filtering, not overall success.

review.scope: Targeted exact-edition success audit; construction and parameter-specific defining passages, not a new full-paper audit.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4 Table2; pp.16–17 Section5.3 and Algorithm, full master-key recovery via AES-128 schedule.
evidence.interpretation: Primary result, model and accounting passages checked; selected-endpoint extraction, not a completed full-paper/forward-literature audit.

evidence.locator: Original PDF p.4 Table 2; pp.16–17 Section 5.3, including p.17 explicit replay without terminal MixColumns, eleven-step recovery, and experimental check.
evidence.interpretation: Independently confirms full ten-round AES-128 with one unknown nonzero byte fault in known byte 0 before round 8; output pairing is required. Final three-round working window is not a three-round ordinary AES endpoint. 2^16 surviving candidates are not a success probability.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.16–17 /printed184–185 Section5.3, Lemma3 and complete11-step fault procedure.
evidence.interpretation: The source reports an implemented fault attack and the expected2^16 tested candidates, but no number of attack trials, population success fraction or probability of unique correct-key recovery. The counts2^16/2^24 describe intermediate filtering, not overall success.

limitations: All 19 original pages read and result inventory independently checked; bounded version/forward checks completed. No author solver, attack code, or numerical success experiment executed.
